extracted.intended_audience: clinical trial protocol writers and trial teams (investigators, statisticians, trial coordinators, PPI contributors) responsible for including patient-reported outcomes (PROs) in protocols
extracted.subtask_description: A protocol-template / checklist for drafting and reviewing the patient-reported outcomes (PRO) sections of clinical trial protocols, covering rationale, measures, administration, monitoring, statistical analysis, and operational details.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRO content author (SPIRIT-5a-PRO Elaboration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the individual(s) responsible for the PRO content of the trial protocol (name, affiliation(s), telephone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing information on who wrote the PRO-specific aspects promotes transparency and accountability and identifies the appropriate point of contact for resolution of PRO queries. Document patient contributions where applicable. The PRO author should be part of the protocol writing committee and ensure PROs are harmonized with other clinical endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol synopsis with PRO-specific information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a short (1–2 page) protocol synopsis that contains the key protocol points including PRO-specific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete this section after the main text to ensure consistency with the main protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Activities (SoA) for PRO assessments (SPIRIT-13-PRO Extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a schedule of PRO assessments, provide a rationale for the time points, and justify if the initial assessment is not pre-randomization; specify time windows, whether PRO collection is prior to clinical assessments, and order of administration if multiple questionnaires are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarise PRO schedule alongside other trial assessments in a table. Ideally show assessments in the order they will be completed. If more than one PRO measure is used, specify each on separate lines if administered at different times. Baseline PROs should be completed prior to randomization; ensure recall periods and windowing do not overlap trial day 0. State whether PROs will be collected after disease progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRO-specific study rationale (SPIRIT-6a-PRO Extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the PRO-specific research question and rationale for PRO assessment and summarize PRO findings in relevant studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clearly defined question helps with selection of measures and specification of hypotheses and analyses. When the PRO is a secondary or exploratory outcome, a brief rationale may suffice. Provide detailed information in the scientific rationale section if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives and PRO endpoints (SPIRIT-7 & SPIRIT-12-PRO Extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific PRO objectives (including relevant PRO concepts/domains) and specify for each PRO endpoint the concept/domain, analysis metric (e.g., change from baseline, final value, time-to-event) and the principal time point or period of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether PRO domains/time points are confirmatory, descriptive or exploratory. Align PRO endpoints closely with trial objectives; pre-specify domains and principal time points to reduce multiple testing and selective reporting. Include utility measures (e.g., EQ-5D) if relevant to cost-utility analyses. Where objectives are confirmatory, specify if superiority, equivalence, or non-inferiority is intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific rationale for study design (PRO-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how PRO evaluation aligns with the overall trial design and present detailed PRO-specific rationale (including summary of PRO findings in relevant studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate how the PRO design addresses the research objectives. Detailed information not included in the short rationale (Section 2.1.1) should be provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRO-specific eligibility criteria (SPIRIT-10-PRO Extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify any PRO-specific eligibility criteria (e.g., language/reading requirements or pre-randomization completion of PRO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PROs will not be collected from the entire sample, provide rationale and describe sampling method for PRO subsamples. Provide translated PRO versions where needed or specify reasons for not providing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRO capture method involving a medical device
rubrics_metrics.description: If ePRO systems or other PRO capture tools meet the definition of a medical device (e.g., provide actionable alerts), refer to the relevant regulatory directive for that jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that some ePROs may be regulated as medical devices and require adherence to applicable device regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRO assessment for participants who discontinue or deviate (SPIRIT-18b (ii)-PRO Elaboration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the process of PRO assessment for participants who discontinue or deviate from the assigned intervention protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide procedures to collect PROs from participants who withdraw early (e.g., pre-paid packaging to return PRO assessments or ePRO devices). A clear plan minimizes bias and helps ensure standardized and timely collection of required PRO data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify PRO hypotheses (SPIRIT-7-PRO Extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the PRO hypotheses and whether the objective is to support superiority, equivalence or non-inferiority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specification encourages identification of key PRO domains and time points and reduces the risk of multiple statistical testing and selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify PRO instrument selection and describe measurement properties (SPIRIT-18a (i)-PRO Extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify the PRO instrument to be used and describe domains, number of items, recall period, instrument scaling and scoring (range and direction), and provide evidence of measurement properties, interpretation guidelines, and patient acceptability/burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide or cite validation evidence, ideally in the target population. State whether the measure will be used per user manual and justify any deviations. Interpretation guidelines should include pre-defined clinical relevance thresholds, preferably population-specific. Consider patient burden (time, cognitive, emotional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of administration and setting (SPIRIT-18a (ii)-PRO Extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a data collection plan outlining permitted modes of administration (paper, telephone, electronic, other) and setting (clinic, home, other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether site-based assessments must be completed prior to other assessments or discussions. Provide quiet space and time for participants. Describe procedures if electronic tools are unavailable or lost. Consider evidence of equivalence between modes (usability testing, cognitive debriefing) if changing mode from validated versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategies to minimize avoidable missing PRO data (SPIRIT-18b (i)-PRO Extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify PRO data collection and management strategies for minimizing avoidable missing data and signpost to the statistical analysis plan as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect reasons for missed assessments (e.g., via CRFs). Common avoidable causes include administrative errors, lack of explanation of importance, and overly burdensome questionnaires. Protocol content examples: clearly define PRO endpoints/hypotheses, provide rationale, specify time points and acceptable windows, align with clinic visits, minimize burden, and specify the importance of complete PRO data. Consult SISAQOL, CONSORT-PRO and PROTEUS for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language versions and translation/cultural adaptation (SPIRIT-18a (iii)-PRO Extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify whether more than one language version will be used and state whether translated versions have been developed using recommended methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate translation and cultural adaptation methodology for multinational or multi-language trials; cite references when available. Lack of translations should be justified and implications for inclusivity noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy-reported outcomes (SPIRIT-18a (iv)-PRO Extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: State and justify the use of a proxy respondent when someone other than the participant must answer on their behalf, and provide or cite evidence of validity of proxy assessment if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate proxy reporting from assistance (someone helping a participant to respond). If used, ideally have the same proxy person throughout the trial to reduce variability and document justification to allow assessment of potential bias and facilitate CONSORT-PRO reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring of PRO data for safety (SPIRIT-22-PRO Extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether PRO data will be monitored during the study to inform clinical care of individual participants and, if so, how this will be managed and explained to participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PROs replace or augment solicited AE recording, they should be recognised within safety monitoring procedures. Specify monitoring plans (or explicitly state if monitoring is not planned) and outline alternative support mechanisms. Planning protects participant interests and helps minimise bias arising from variable alert management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and power considerations when PRO is primary endpoint (SPIRIT-14-PRO Elaboration)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a PRO is the primary endpoint, state the required sample size (and how it was determined) and recruitment targets accounting for expected loss to follow-up; if not driven by PRO, discuss power for principal PRO analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify criteria for clinical significance (e.g., minimal important difference, responder definition) when known. Provide enough information on secondary/tertiary/exploratory PROs to justify inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRO statistical analysis methods and multiplicity control (SPIRIT-20a-PRO Elaboration)
rubrics_metrics.description: State PRO analysis methods, including plans for addressing multiplicity/type I (α) error and pre-defined clinical relevance thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods should align with specified endpoints and reflect superiority/equivalence/non-inferiority objectives. Pre-specify key PRO domain(s) and principal time point(s). Describe methods to control multiplicity (stepwise/sequential testing, Bonferroni, etc.) or explicitly state if no plans exist. Provide summary in protocol with full details in the statistical analysis plan; pre-specify sensitivity analyses where planned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and description of missing PRO data (SPIRIT-20c-PRO Elaboration)
rubrics_metrics.description: State how missing data will be described and outline methods for handling missing items or entire assessments (e.g., imputation approaches and sensitivity analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish item-level vs entire-assessment missingness and intermittent vs lost-to-follow-up. State how missing PRO data will be recorded and categorised. Acknowledge missing data mechanisms and the assumptions of statistical approaches; inappropriate method selection can bias results. Consult SISAQOL for guidance and provide full details in the SAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychometric and additional PRO analyses (9.1.2 Other Analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge any planned psychometric analyses of the PRO measure(s) or additional research questions using PRO data, with reference to the statistical analysis plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If psychometric work is planned (reliability, validity, responsiveness), state it in the protocol and reference methods and SAP or other detailed documents (e.g., Calvert et al. 2018 JAMA Supplement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication policy and reporting (10.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: State publication policy for PRO data and commit to reporting according to CONSORT and CONSORT-PRO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence shows PRO data are underreported; protocol should state publication plans and adhere to CONSORT-PRO. Depending on mode of administration, include paper copies or screenshots of ePRO instruments as good practice. Include copyright and version information and acknowledge permissions required for instrument use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: copies of PRO instruments and operational documentation (10.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Append copies (or screenshots) of PRO instruments with copyright/version information and documentation supporting their use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including instrument copies and documentation supports standardised administration and scoring; show acknowledgements for instruments requiring permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise specification of endpoints from PRO data
rubrics_metrics.description: Define endpoints precisely from PRO data by specifying measurement variable, analysis metric, method of aggregation, and time point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An endpoint typically specifies assessment type, timing, tools used, how multiple assessments are combined and aggregated (e.g., change from baseline at 6 weeks in mean fatigue score). Several endpoints can be derived from the same outcome source data; be explicit to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and procedures for mode equivalence (electronic vs paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and document evidence of equivalence between electronic and paper modes of administration when using electronic PROs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If electronic PRO measures contain only minor modifications relative to paper versions, usability testing and cognitive debriefing may suffice. Cite ISPOR ePRO Good Research Practices and other evidence where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording reasons for missed PRO assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and document reasons for missed PRO assessments during the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document reasons in CRFs to facilitate analysis of missingness and inform strategies to reduce avoidable missing data.
